correctness.rationale: Tafazolian Prop. 8.2 applies geometrically with p≥5 and c≠0. Independently, for z=2x−(y^p−y) the quadratic cover is branched at the simple roots of f(y)=y^(2p)−2y^(p+1)+y²−4c. Any nonaffine Möbius map preserving those roots has finite pole q and sends their sum to zero. Writing it as α+β/(y−q), the transformed sum forces f′(q)=0 (q is not a branch point), hence q∈F_p; the inverse likewise puts α∈F_p. Composing with translations reduces to y↦β/y, contradicted by the nonzero degree-(2p−2) term of y^(2p)f(β/y), absent in f for p≥5. For an affine map, comparing coefficients of y^(p+1), y^p and 1 shows the multiplier is ±1 and the shift is in F_p. The hyperelliptic involution provides the central kernel and translations/sign lift over F_p. Thus the full group is constant C₂×D_(2p); its conjugacy classes give (p+1) rotation/central types plus two reflection types. The Artin–Schreier shift and nonsquare quadratic descent realize the A and B types, and x=−δX,y=δY with δ²=d and δ^p=−δ realizes the sign twist R; a further central quadratic descent realizes S. These account for every class, independently of coincidences among point counts. Two simple poles give genus and geometric p-rank both p−1. A,R have one rational point over each of 0,∞ by total ramification; B,S have no rational point at infinity because their even-degree hyperelliptic polynomials have nonsquare leading coefficient after dividing by d. For finite coordinates the A quadratic discriminant gives p(1+χ), B gives p(1−χ), R gives one solution for each nonzero X, and S uses the complete quadratic character sum −1. The latter follows from counting factorizations (t−z)(t+z)=b≠0; separating a=0 at value χ(−c) and pairing a with −a gives all three frequencies. Choosing t∈F_p^× with t²≠c yields a nonzero square discriminant and a pointless B twist. The finite supplied verifier was inspected but not executed; these checks establish the all-prime scope analytically.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification problem for an ordinary genus-(p−1) Artin–Schreier curve, where geometric isomorphism does not settle even rational point existence. The explicit models and their exact frequencies determine which point counts can be realized by descent, including a pointless form for every allowed c. The value lies in the complete constructive spectrum rather than just counting conjugacy classes or applying a single character sum.
